title: Naturality of the projection-and-counit tensor transpose
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, $q=p^a$ with $a\ge1$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\ge1$. Put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-pur-conventions]. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$ a smooth separated finite-type $k$-morphism of pure relative dimension $d\ge0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Use the ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories on the small pro-etale sites, the derived pullback and tensor, and the constructible exceptional functor $Rf^!$ [def-pur-co-smoothness]. Put $\omega_f=Rf^!A_Y$.
For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$, the bounded constructible finite-Tor subcategory, put $M_K=Lf^*K$ and let $\theta_{f,K}:M_K\otimes_A^L\omega_f\to Rf^!K$ be the specified map of [def-pur-co-smoothness]: the transpose under the bounded etale-origin compact-support Hom bijection of tensor symmetry, $\operatorname{PF}_{f,\omega_f,K}^{-1}$, $\varepsilon_{f,A_Y}\otimes1_K$, and the left unitor. For every morphism $u:K\to K'$ of this subcategory, with $m=Lf^*u$, one has the equality of derived morphisms
$$Rf^!u\circ\theta_{f,K}=\theta_{f,K'}\circ(m\otimes1_{\omega_f}).$$
Equivalently, writing $a_K:Rf_!(M_K\otimes^L\omega_f)\to K$ for the displayed transpose input, its coefficient square is
$$u\circ a_K=a_{K'}\circ Rf_!(m\otimes1_{\omega_f}).$$
No Tate orientation or smooth purity map occurs in this assertion.

proof.text: Write $F=Rf_!$, $H=Rf^!$, $\Omega=HA_Y$, $T_K=M_K\otimes_A^L\Omega$, and $t=m\otimes1_\Omega:T_K\to T_{K'}$. The constant unit $A_Y$ is bounded constructible of Tor amplitude $[0,0]$. By [thm-sf-preservation-class](1), $\Omega$ is bounded constructible; by [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude], $M_K,M_{K'}$ are bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude. Hence [lem-sf-tensor-ctf](i) puts $T_K,T_{K'}$ in the bounded constructible category. These are precisely the source inputs of the specified bounded etale-origin Hom bijection used in [def-pur-co-smoothness]. Write $s_K:M_K\otimes\Omega\to\Omega\otimes M_K$ for symmetry, $P_K=\operatorname{PF}_{f,\Omega,K}$, $e=\varepsilon_{f,A_Y}:F\Omega\to A_Y$, and $\lambda_K:A_Y\otimes K\to K$ for the left unitor. The definition gives $a_K=\lambda_K\circ(e\otimes1_K)\circ P_K^{-1}\circ F(s_K)$ and $\theta_{f,K}=\Phi_{T_K,K}(a_K)$, where $\Phi$ denotes that Hom bijection. All tensors below are derived.

source.place: First sentence, naturality of the tensor formula; returned proof step 1.

proof.text: The tensor of [def-pur-co-smoothness] is the K-flat model $P\otimes K_2$ of [def-weil-derived-tensor]. By [lem-sf-ringed-derived-native-tensor] the native derived tensor is symmetric monoidal, and its natural comparison $Q(\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes L))\cong Q(P)\otimes Q(L)$ with this model agrees with the K-flat comparisons and preserves the braiding and both unitors. Transporting along it, the model's symmetry and left unitor are natural transformations and the model is a bifunctor (interchange law). Naturality of the symmetry gives $s_{K'}\circ t=(1_\Omega\otimes m)\circ s_K$. The projection isomorphisms are natural in the coefficient variable by [fix-prop-projection-formula], applied with first input $\Omega\in D^b_c(X,A)$ and second inputs $K,K'\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$. Thus $F(1_\Omega\otimes m)\circ P_K=P_{K'}\circ(1_{F\Omega}\otimes u)$. Composing with the two inverses gives $P_{K'}^{-1}\circ F(1_\Omega\otimes m)=(1_{F\Omega}\otimes u)\circ P_K^{-1}$. Put $b_K=P_K^{-1}\circ F(s_K)$. Functoriality of $F$ and the symmetry equation now give $b_{K'}\circ F(t)=(1_{F\Omega}\otimes u)\circ b_K$.

source.place: First sentence, naturality of the tensor formula; returned proof step 1.

proof.text:
Bifunctoriality of the model tensor and naturality of its left unitor, transported in Step 2 from [lem-sf-ringed-derived-native-tensor], give $(e\otimes1_{K'})\circ(1_{F\Omega}\otimes u)=(1_{A_Y}\otimes u)\circ(e\otimes1_K)$ and $\lambda_{K'}\circ(1_{A_Y}\otimes u)=u\circ\lambda_K$. Substitute the equation for $b$ from Step 2 into the defining composite of [def-pur-co-smoothness]:
$$a_{K'}\circ F(t)=\lambda_{K'}\circ(e\otimes1_{K'})\circ(1_{F\Omega}\otimes u)\circ b_K=u\circ\lambda_K\circ(e\otimes1_K)\circ b_K=u\circ a_K.$$
This is the coefficient square in the statement.

source.place: First sentence, naturality of the tensor formula; returned proof step 1.

proof.text:
Use the natural Hom bijection of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class](2), on the bounded constructible inputs checked in Step 1, and the specified transpose of [def-pur-co-smoothness]. Its naturality in the target and source respectively gives
$$\Phi_{T_K,K'}(u\circ a_K)=H(u)\circ\Phi_{T_K,K}(a_K)=H(u)\circ\theta_{f,K},$$
$$\Phi_{T_K,K'}(a_{K'}\circ F(t))=\Phi_{T_{K'},K'}(a_{K'})\circ t=\theta_{f,K'}\circ t.$$
Apply this one bijection to the equality in Step 3 to obtain $Rf^!u\circ\theta_{f,K}=\theta_{f,K'}\circ(m\otimes1_\Omega)$. Conversely its injectivity recovers Step 3 from this equality, proving the claimed equivalence. Only its stated bounded comparison domain is used.
